text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. The main goal is readability, meaning that anyone can understand your code just by reading it, without needing lengthy explanations. A crucial part of this is following clear naming conventions; variables and functions should have names that describe their purpose, like `calculateTotalPrice` instead of `calc` or `x`. Keeping your functions small and focused on a single task makes the code easier to test and debug. Ultimately, clean code is about maintainability. Since software is constantly updated, writing code that is simple and organized saves time and effort for future developers, including yourself.
